stumbles.quote: The 3-bit and 4-bit codes beat the live index in fewer bytes.
stumbles.why: The 3-bit code takes 104 bytes and the 4-bit code takes 136 bytes. Both are fewer than 200, but the byte sizes don't obviously match the bit math (256×3 bits is 96 bytes). The extra bytes are unexplained.

point: Folding Ettin-17m's output matrix to 256 dimensions leaves float search unchanged, and 3–4 bit quantized codes on those dimensions beat the current 2-bit 768-dimensional index. At the same bit width, though, the 256-dimensional codes do worse.
